test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 11 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: One pipe can fill the tank in 19 minutes while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 21 minutes. If both the pipes are operated together on empty tank, how long (in minutes) will it take to fill two-third of the tank?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Net filling efficiency per minute = 1/19 − 1/21 = (21 − 19) / (19 × 21) = 2 / 399

Time to fill full tank = 399 / 2 minutes

Time to fill 2/3rd tank = (399 / 2) × (2 / 3) = 133 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 133 minutes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling time = 19 minutes, Emptying time = 21 minutes.

**Formula Used:** Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 
 **Pipe Type** **Time (min)** **Total Capacity (LCM)** **Efficiency** 
 **Filling Pipe** 19 399 +21 
 **Emptying Pipe** 21 −19 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Net efficiency of both pipes = 21 − 19 = 2 units/min

⇒ Required work = 2/3 of Total Capacity = (2/3) × 399 = 266 units

⇒ Required time = Required work ÷ Net efficiency

⇒ Required time = 266 ÷ 2 = 133 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 133 minutes.**

**__Additional Information__**

Net Rate of Flow

When one pipe fills (rate x) and another empties (rate y), the combined rate is (1/x − 1/y) per unit time.

Pipes and Cisterns Logic

Inlet pipes contribute positive work (+) while Outlet pipes contribute negative work (−) towards filling the tank.

Partial Filling

Time taken to fill 'k' fraction of a tank = (k × Total Capacity) ÷ Net Efficiency.</p
